definition: In artificial intelligence, the distributed multi-agent reasoning system (dMARS) was a platform for intelligent software agents developed at the AAII that makes uses of the belief–desire–intention software model (BDI).
details: The design for dMARS was an extension of the intelligent agent cognitive architecture developed at SRI International called procedural reasoning system (PRS). The most recent incarnation of this framework is the JACK Intelligent Agents platform.
story: Picture hiring a brilliant new assistant on their first morning — smart, motivated, but with no idea how anything in your office actually works. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. It is the difference between a search engine and a helper who actually finishes the task. It is a loop of look, act, and learn — the same way you cook from a recipe you have never tried: add, taste, correct. And that habit of checking, acting, then checking again is Distributed multi-agent reasoning system.
